newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Albright says Iraq, not UN, preventing oil plan.
newsitem.headline: Albright says Iraq, not UN, preventing oil plan.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright said Thursady that Iraq, not the United Nations, was preventing the oil-for-food swap that had been scheduled for last month.
Speaking to reporters after a Security Council meeting, she said the U.S. was concerned at the delay in carrying out resolution 986, which sets terms for the swap.

"We are concerned about 986 and believe it is not the United Nations that is keeping that resolution from coming into play but it is coming from Baghdad. We continue to be concerned about the people of Iraq and hope very much that 986 will be able to be complied with," Albright said.
She was referring to Iraqi conditions on U.N. monitors distributing food supplies, particularly in the Kurdish north where Baghdad has demanded prior notice of their movements.

The plan was approved last May 20 and enables Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy food, medicines and other humanitarian supplies. It was to go into effect early in September but was delayed because of fighting among Kurdish factions and Iraqi troops aiding one Kurdish faction.
